newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore manufacturers in S$150 mln China project.
newsitem.headline: Singapore manufacturers in S$150 mln China project.

text.p: The Singapore Confederation of Industries (SCI) said on Thursday it has signed an agreement to develop a site in China's Qingdao Industrial Park at a cost of Singapore $150 million.
SCI said in a statement it hoped the site would initially attract S$500 million worth of manufacturing investment.
SCI had agreed on a 50-year lease of the three square km site, which would be developed in three phases over eight years into a modern industrial park for advanced technology industries.
The agreement was signed with the Qingdao Hi-Tech Park Authority of the Qingdao City Government.

A joint venture company, Union Bright Investment Pte Ltd, has been set up to develop the project. It is jointly owned by SCI's investment arm Manufacturers Investment Holdings Ltd and Grandlink Group Pte Ltd, a consortium of Singapore-based property developers.

The 1,500 member manufacturers' association SCI said the Qingdao Singapore Industrial Park would form part of the larger Qingdao Hi-Tech Park, a comprehensive township development of 67 km being actively developed by the Qingdao City government. Qingdao is in China's northern province of Shangdong.
